title: Cost of the low degree estimator
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $\varepsilon$ be a positive learning parameter, and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. If the estimator’s work bound is at most a natural number $B$, then every outcome in the support of its run on $f$ uses at most $B$ random examples, makes no membership queries, and has charged work at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the low degree learner work cost is at most $B$
the outcome belongs to the support of the estimator’s run on the target
